analysis.investment_thesis: KSB is a genuinely high-quality industrial business — zero debt, 14% revenue CAGR, 18.3% ROE, and a reputable German promoter holding 69.8% — exactly the kind of steady compounder I respect. However, at 58x P/E and near-zero FCF yield (~0.5%), the market has priced in decades of perfection, leaving no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Fortress balance sheet — borrowings of just INR 5 Cr against equity of INR 1,679 Cr; D/E effectively zero
Consistent 9-year revenue CAGR of 14% and net profit CAGR of 16.4% — no erratic years, exactly the steady compounding I like
Promoter holding at 69.8% with German parent KSB SE — aligned, reputable, long-term owners
key_risks: Valuation is dangerous — P/E of 58x and EV/EBITDA of 44x are 3x my acceptable ceiling; even a re-rating to 30x means 50% downside
FCF has collapsed — 2025 FCF is effectively zero (INR 0 Cr) and 2022 was negative (-67 Cr); OCF fell sharply to 93 Cr in 2025 from 187 Cr in 2024
Cyclical industrial sector with government capex dependency — pumps/valves demand can slow sharply if infrastructure spending decelerates
red_flags: FCF yield of ~0.5% against my required minimum of 5% — I am paying 10x fair entry price on this metric
Rising CWIP from INR 25 Cr (2022) to INR 89 Cr (2025) signals heavy ongoing capex; returns on new capital deployment unproven
P/B of 10x on an asset-heavy industrial company — this is speculation, not investing
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KSB Limited is a textbook quality industrial business that I admire from a distance. The balance sheet is impeccable — essentially zero debt for the last four years, reserves compounding steadily from INR 856 Cr to INR 1,644 Cr, and ROCE of 24.5% that would make most businesses envious. Revenue has grown from INR 826 Cr to INR 2,696 Cr over nine years at 14% CAGR without a single bad year — even 2020 (INR 1,208 Cr from INR 1,294 Cr) showed resilience. The German promoter holding 69.8% gives me comfort on governance, and operating margins have expanded consistently from ~12.8% in 2016 to 14.5% today. This is exactly the kind of boring, steady compounder I like to own.

However, my job is not just to find good businesses — it is to buy them at prices that protect my capital. At 58x trailing P/E and 44x EV/EBITDA, the market is extrapolating 20+ years of perfection into today's price. I paid low P/E multiples to build DMart into what it is; I did not overpay even for my own business. The free cash flow situation is alarming — 2025 FCF is nil, 2022 was deeply negative, and the FCF yield on a INR 16,850 Cr market cap is below 1%. This is a business worth watching carefully. If the market ever corrects this to 20-25x earnings — around INR 300-350 per share — I would be a serious buyer. At INR 968, I must pass.
